prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: [验证] 中文 · 员工花名册 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "工号" · longest unbreakable unit 53px · widest one-line content 53px
  col 2: header "姓名" · longest unbreakable unit 16px · widest one-line content 62px
  col 3: header "部门" · longest unbreakable unit 16px · widest one-line content 77px
  col 4: header "职级" · longest unbreakable unit 19px · widest one-line content 31px
  col 5: header "入职日期" · longest unbreakable unit 43px · widest one-line content 85px
  col 6: header "主要职责" · longest unbreakable unit 31px · widest one-line content 491px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 360px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 360px wide (column widths sum to at most 359px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 360px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Candidate layouts, rendered in a real browser, shown after the overview: Layout Q, s0A, s1B, s1C, Layout P, Layout R.
Measured facts:
Layout Q: column widths [74, 53, 53, 40, 56, 83] px · table 360×823 px · row heights [60, 199, 83, 176, 199, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 2/6 · tallest cell 8 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 10 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)
s0A: column widths [74, 53, 53, 40, 57, 82] px · table 360×986 px · row heights [60, 269, 83, 222, 246, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 3/6 · tallest cell 11 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 15 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)
s1B: column widths [74, 48, 48, 40, 64, 85] px · table 360×893 px · row heights [60, 199, 129, 176, 199, 129] · column headers on >1 line: 4/6 · tallest cell 8 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 22 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)
s1C: column widths [74, 48, 48, 51, 64, 74] px · table 360×1056 px · row heights [60, 269, 129, 222, 246, 129] · column headers on >1 line: 5/6 · tallest cell 11 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 27 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout P: column widths [74, 53, 53, 40, 55, 84] px · table 360×846 px · row heights [60, 199, 106, 176, 199, 106] · column headers on >1 line: 2/6 · tallest cell 8 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 12 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout R: column widths [74, 53, 53, 40, 64, 75] px · table 360×963 px · row heights [60, 269, 83, 222, 246, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 3/6 · tallest cell 11 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 13 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)

Decide as the responsible designer:
- "finalists": up to 3 layouts you would submit for independent acceptance, best first (more than one only if genuinely different and comparably good);
- "acceptable": others a careful designer would still publish;
- "bad": layouts with clear faults, each with the fault;
- "contrast": ONE deliberately flawed but plausible layout (widths) that a hurried designer might produce, and what is wrong with it;
- "same_function_groups": groups of columns (1-based) that play the same role, and whether they should share a scale here;
- "rationale" (2–4 concrete sentences), "principles" {general: [likely to hold for other tables], specific: [this case only]}, "tradeoffs", "uncertain".
Reply ONLY JSON: {"finalists":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"layout":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""},"same_function_groups":[{"columns":[1,2],"same_scale":true,"why":""}],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}
